pitch_detail.notes: Follows a pleasant left-facing corner crack. Once the crack runs out, bolts lead up and rightward to a ledge with a bolted belay. Mildly runout in places.

Leaves the ledge into a steep left-facing corner with a short 5.6 runout section below a stance for good cams. The climbing then sustains; either run out the hard part or slow down placing extra gear. Ends at a two-bolt belay. Both pitches can be combined, though a 70 m rope then needs two lowers.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches with grades and lengths (50 ft, 80 ft). No rappel table: text gives no stations.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts from a two-bolt ground anchor atop a steep gully; a No. 1 cam fits before the first bolt. Face and crack systems lead up and left passing two further bolts and abundant protection, and tops out on a level shelf where the buttress ends.

Straight up from the ledge with a few pieces before the second bolt, then big jugs through an overhanging roof. Escape left onto the face, clip the bolt at the foot of a large hanging corner and pull the crux there (a No. 3 cam helps). More good gear in the corner crack, then right beneath a nose-shaped block to an optional belay on a slanting ledge with four bolts. The Puff of Smoke variation goes left into a v-groove here.
Can be joined with the pitch below, or belay at the optional anchor. Two bolts lead straight up into a crux roof pull, then easier ground to a two-bolt belay on a comfortable incut ledge.

Step right off the anchor and follow cracks up and right onto an exposed face. Three bolts protect cruxy moves toward a corner; once it gets grassy, move left past a little roof at the arete, take the final bolt, and arrive at a ledge anchor.

review.changed: Four pitches with grades and lengths (feet converted). Rappel info is a general description, not a station list, so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin up the first few bolts of the neighbouring route, then duck left into a crack to the first belay of Hidden Treasure. Return right onto steep bolted face and laybacks with some gear, gain a ledge system and ramp, then work stemming moves up a shallow dihedral (the hardest bit of the pitch) to the belay. Bring a #1 cam and a couple of finger-size pieces.

Easy ground leads to a ledge beneath a hanging arete. Fully bolted: take care when belaying the second clip, there is a rest out right at the third bolt, and the finishing moves to the chains are exposed and mentally demanding.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches without grades or lengths (text gives none).

pitch_detail.notes: Cracks for about 25 feet to a grassy ledge, then bridging up a dihedral past three bolts. Move right onto a rounded arete for the hardest moves and continue to a comfortable belay ledge.

A bolt just off the belay starts a mix of face moves and finger cracks heading left, ending in a chimney-like slot. Juggy bolted face follows to a two-bolt belay left of a neighbouring route's second pitch, a safer stance should anything fall.

The best pitch: rise up and right from the belay, crossing the corner system of a neighbouring route. Technical corner work drifts right again to exposed finishing moves on solid granite. Belay at the top or lower from the hooks to the rappel station below.

review.changed: Three pitches with grades; no lengths given.

pitch_detail.notes: After moving right along a tree ledge you look up into the gully system. This pitch may be mixed climbing depending on conditions, described as feeling like easy fifth class.
Climbs the main flow that descends on the left of the gully.

review.changed: Two pitches described briefly; text calls the climb about 2000 ft of ice leading up to the cliffs, so the two listed pitches cover only the headwall flows.
review.other_findings: Stored length 762 m versus text describing only two pitches on a 2000 ft route; stored grade lists 5.8 which text does not mention.

pitch_detail.notes: Two starts. Variation 1a: flaring corner with two bolts (5.9), about 20 feet of unprotected slab to a third bolt, then right with two more clips (5.8) to a ledge anchor under the headwall. Variation 1b starts higher, climbs an easy headwall and joins 1a at its fourth bolt.

From the anchor go up and right to a fixed pin at the headwall base, then straight up vertical rock to a bolt. A cam can substitute for a missing pin to reach a jug. Step left up a layback flake to a two-bolt belay in a water hole.

Runout climbing straight up with occasional gear toward a pair of bolts level with a tree ledge on the right. Extend a runner on one of them, then walk the easy traverse right to a rappel anchor with two bolts.
Traditionally placed bolts on slab, following bolts and one fixed pin to a two-bolt rappel anchor.

review.changed: Four pitches; pitch 2 grade not stated (only called the crux). Rappel text is a rope-length note, not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Direct start from a lone bolt: climb up and right past bolts to a moderate crack and right-facing corner, then move left to another crack and straight up to a two-bolt belay.

Step right into a corner to an obvious chockstone and pull awkwardly over it. Leave the corner, step right and climb a steep exposed face, staying left of loose rock to a two-bolt rappel anchor atop the buttress.

review.changed: Two pitches (80 ft, 120 ft); no per-pitch grades given.

pitch_detail.notes: Climbs the right-facing dihedral to a ledge around 120 feet up. Build the anchor in the finger crack. The route can also be done as one long pitch.
Follows the corner until it ends then finishes left on the buttress to a slung block marking the top.

review.changed: Wrote the two-pitch split with only the first length (120 ft); no grades per pitch. Rappel text is not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Wide crack to easier ground, belaying on a comfortable ledge. Watch for loose blocks and back up the anchor.

A long pitch of about 50 m: slab to a roof, skirt it right and climb a cleaved flake to a bolt with slings. Lower about 15 feet and pendulum right to a stance under a large left-facing corner, then follow a thin finger crack in the left wall, the technical crux. Belay from two bolts at an awkward stance. Double ropes cut drag.
Committing moves right off the belay and a big reach to a crack that widens through a bulge to a stance below the wide crack. Short, and can be linked with the next pitch.
The Half Moon Crack: simply follow the wide crack. Gear only at the start, then none; the last moves steepen and trend right. A fall would hit the slab below.

review.changed: Four pitches with grades; descent is three double-rope raps but no stations listed, so no table.

pitch_detail.notes: Hand and fist crack trending up and left to a large grassy ledge.
Splitter hand crack to a pin anchor; fairly short.
Crack continues, thinning near the top to thin hands and a lieback; rated harder by some than others. Short, and could link with pitch 2.
Continues the crack through a short roof; short pitch.
Parallel cracks above the belay: mostly the left, using the right as needed, stemming and jamming.
Leave the belay through a short roof crack on knobs, rest, then splitter hand and finger crack above. Rated lower than topo grades by the parties who climbed it.
Climb 10-15 feet above the belay then traverse a rail left into a corner crack.
Leave the ramp by a tidy corner, reach grassy blocks leftward, then a vegetated ledge and a fixed belay under a chimney.
Loose chimney, then right up a black-streaked corner and out left on a hand crack to a grassy ledge with an anchor.
Wander grassy ledges up and right to a bolted anchor.
The standard finish goes up the splitter and arete above (not described in detail); the alternative is easy, loose, blocky ground around the corner to the right to the summit.

review.changed: All 11 pitches; grades as reported (several uncertain, hedged). No rappel table: descent is a general note.
review.other_findings: Stored grade 5.12b; text puts crux around 12a/b.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts in a wide easy corner at the notch, then mossy face to a small ledge; a nut marks the last rappel.
Flakes and face angling up beside a big blocky feature to the left, toward a weakness higher up; a slung horn marks a rappel. Move the belay above loose rock to the next face.
Fun cracks aiming for the top and easier ground.
Easy fifth-class ground along the ridge to the summit block.

review.changed: Four pitches; the descent is retracing the route using fixed stations in the gully.

pitch_detail.notes: Left-facing corner to a fixed belay.
Continue the corner to a fixed belay.
Follow the corner to its end and exit right below a large roof. Often wet; dry, the exit moves feel about 5.10a.
Wander up the face to the foot of a long chimney.
The long, secure chimney. Simul-climbing is advisable, especially for a one-day ascent.
Wander up and right to a huge flat ledge, an excellent bivy.
Big left-facing corner to a small ledge at the edge of the face.
Parallel cracks up the face; abundant knobs encourage face climbing. Many ways to go, ending at the base of an unmistakable roof.

Past the obvious three-foot roof, a pull much harder than anything else on the route, easily aided at C1, otherwise about 5.11-. A splitter hand crack through the roof to the right is an alternative. Sustained 5.9 cracks lead to the belay.
Gradually widening cracks to the summit; the last pitch has easy offwidth.

review.changed: All 18 pitches covered as ranges where text groups them. Descent is a rap route with stations hard to find; no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Ramp and third-class holds right for nearly 10 m to the first bolt, then a few bolts straight up and a steep headwall on large holds to a ledge anchor.

Traverse left off the belay to a large flake, then a boulder problem through three bolts on pockets and edges. Stand to rest, continue on incut edges to a final traverse, belaying on top of the pillar.
Slab on featured rock; the crux is cresting a bulge after easier climbing, then bolts to another anchor ledge.
Easy climbing on big holds and rolling rock; likely linkable with the third pitch.
Similar easy climbing until a 10-foot headwall where holds thin, then a scramble to the summit anchor.

review.changed: Five pitches with grades and lengths. Descent: walk off preferred; no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Clip the first bolt of the neighbouring route, traverse left on a grassy ledge, up a pocketed water streak and step left onto the arete. Belay on a ledge.

Fourth class for about 40 feet on top of a separated flake to an overhung bulge. Pull on sidepulls and pinches, a big undercling gives a rest before roughly 20 feet more of 5.10 face, and finish left across a mossy runnel to a large ledge.

Head left over moss to bolt one, then scramble onto a pillar for brief steep moves. Easy ground reaches a second pillar beside a loose cave, which you cross rightward on small edges before low-angle terrain leads to the belay.
Directly up from the belay ledge across very easy terrain with long runouts: one 5.6 move, then a hike to the top. Beware falling rock on the rope.
Shared with the neighbouring route: 15 m left into the cleft, scramble to a two-bolt belay.

review.changed: Five pitches with grades, lengths, bolts. Rappel option mentioned only.

pitch_detail.notes: Slightly off-vertical rock with short kickbacks; small crimps and rock-overs, then a long stretch of easy but runout climbing to anchors.
Easy runout slab to a headwall with good rock, a telephone hold and deep pockets.
Easy slab to an arete passing a roof, then bolts trending right to the anchor.
About 30 m of fourth-class scrambling with two bolts aiming for the notch at the cleft's rim; bridge the chasm, clip a bolt, commit; the anchor is 5 m above on a large ledge.

review.changed: Four pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: Jugs, pockets, sidepulls and crimps with a small roof and a few cryptic cruxes, finishing on large pockets to a good ledge. Clip the first bolt from a big two-hand pocket.

Juggy lower-angle ground up the right side, then around the corner left to pull a mini roof. Ends below a huge roof; belay right of the anchors on the flake ledge. Can link with pitch 1 using 19 draws.

Thin balancy moves up, traverse left to a massive undercling pocket, then up and left on big jugs to the fourth bolt and back right through cryptic holds and flakes. Cruxes near the start and end. Bring a few extendable draws. Belay on a ledge near the top.

review.changed: Three pitches; all anchors two bolts with rap rings (stated generally in the text).

pitch_detail.notes: Steep ice drip on the left of the first rock band; gets plenty of sun and may be out of condition. A variation takes the narrow gully at the right end. A snowfield climb leads to the base of pitch 2.
Sustained steep ice and mixed climbing starting at the snowfield's upper left, a full 60 m. A snow gully above heads toward the rock band.
Short ice step on the right of the rock band to the upper snow slopes; variations may exist. A snow gully bearing left joins the Wyeast Ridge route near the summit.

review.changed: Three pitches without grades; only P2 length given.

pitch_detail.notes: Obvious narrow ice flow, thin in places.
Straight up the ice to the foot of the hardest pitch.
Mushroom feature, the standout pitch.

review.changed: Three pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: Moderate ice; all pitches here are rope-stretching.
Steep start that soon eases into rolling ice terrain.
Hardest-feeling for sustained effort. At its top, bolts sit on the left by a broad snow ramp; remember them when descending.
Starts with a steep curtain, the crux, then rolling terrain and a short bulge to finish in the trees.

review.changed: Four pitches with grades. No rappel table: descent is a general description.

pitch_detail.notes: Ice up to the foot of a steeper wall of ice.
Continue toward the final pillar, which now looms.
The final pillar: about 50 m of vertical ice.

review.changed: Only pitches 4-6 are described; pitches 1-3 have no text and were not written.
